messages:
sara: Alert — prod-us-east inference cluster showing ~40% throughput drop and latency tail spikes starting ~13:02 UTC. Grafana spike on worker restarts and GPU memory churn. Raising incident. @alex @matt pls investigate :rotating_light:

alex: Looking. Quick check: some workers are repeatedly restarting with GPU OOMs. node=gpu-node-7 shows repeated container OOMKilled events.

matt: I pulled logs from one of the failing pods. Relevant snippet:
```
2026-03-18T13:03:11Z ERROR runtime: allocation failed: out of memory
worker process killed by OOM
stacktrace: ...
```

jorge: Noted. Also seeing lots of small allocations and free cycles on the same GPU between restarts — smells like memory fragmentation rather than a steady leak. nv-hostengine and driver reclaimed memory but the app couldn't satisfy a large contiguous allocation.

alex: Running `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv` shows processes with fragmented usage. Also kernel selection logs show a recent revert fallback to a generic kernel for matmul on the 8-bit quant path (deploy abc123). Could be larger working set for that kernel.

ci-bot: Deploy abc123 -> rollout completed at 2026-03-18T12:58:05Z. Noted.
messages_continued:
jorge: I profiled the runtime immediately after the incident start. Top findings:
- A sudden increase in temporary tensor allocations at generation step ~token 32 due to a batching heuristic change that allowed batch_size up to 32 for low-priority routes.
- Kernel selector opted into the f32 fallback for a subset of layers because the quantized kernel path had a mismatch for sequence_len=1024; that fallback allocs a large work buffer per-thread.

sara: So combination = larger per-request working set + higher batch sizes -> fragmentation -> OOMs and restarts. Any quick mitigations?

alex: Mitigations in progress:
1) Hotpatch: force batcher max_batch=8 via config override (applied to region-us-east) -> rolling update started.
2) Set KV cache eviction aggressive TTL to 30s for the affected model group to reclaim prefix caches.
3) Temporarily pin kernel selection to previous stable commit (kernel-selector v2.4) until we roll a proper fix.

danielle: Rolling override applied. Traffic is being throttled by the API gateway to reduce surge. Observed fewer restarts in the last 3 minutes.

matt: After reducing batch size, worker OOM rate dropped from ~1/min to ~0.05/min. Throughput recovered ~70% of baseline so far. Still seeing some noisy neighbors on gpu-node-9 where other tenants pushed large memory spikes.

jorge: For the long term:
- Revisit batching heuristics: ensure per-model memory estimator uses kernel working set estimates (not just token/batch heuristics).
- Fix kernel selector bug: the quantized path returns incorrect worksize for sequence_len > 512 causing fallback. Need unit test coverage for seq_len matrix.
- Add fragmentation monitoring: track number of allocation failures due to contiguous block requests, and expose in console.

alex: Created a short ticket: INF-3245 (kernel-selector: incorrect worksize for q8 matmul at seq_len>512). Repro script posted in ticket.

sara: Postmortem owners: @jorge (root cause + runtime fix), @matt (operational mitigations + dashboards), @danielle (capacity isolation + gateway throttles).

ops-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 — throughput recovering, mitigation applied.

matt: Notes for the postmortem draft: include timeline, commit abc123 impact, config diff for batcher override, nvidia-smi captures, and sample logs showing allocation failure. I'll attach traces.

jorge: Also propose an automatic fallback policy: if worker experiences >3 contiguous allocation failures within 5m, shrink batcher max and trigger canary kernel-selector rollback automatically.

sara: Agree. For now we keep the override until INF-3245 is fixed and tested. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

alex: Follow-ups: I'll prepare canary rollout for kernel-selector v2.4 -> v2.5 with stronger memory estimates. ETA EOD.

danielle: I'll coordinate capacity rebalancing to move noisy tenants temporarily off gpu-node-9.

sara: Closing slack thread for live updates; will link to postmortem when ready.
